headline: Large User Grid Cost Responsibility
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, primarily data centers, bear the costs of new grid infrastructure required for their operations, preventing these costs from being passed to residential customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor Spanberger's administration, environmental advocates.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia moves to shift more power costs from families to data centers
news_summary: Virginia regulators are shifting the burden of power grid expansion costs to large energy users, such as data centers, to prevent residential customers from paying for infrastructure built solely for data center growth. Governor Spanberger stated this order is projected to save Virginians hundreds of millions of dollars by ensuring data centers pay their full share.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This legislation requires water suppliers to report the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, provided to data centers to the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, local communities.
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law mandates local water authorities to report data center water usage, making the information publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide better data for assessing regional water supply risk and holding the industry accountable.

headline: Local Data Center Siting Rules
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential units and schools for new high energy use facilities and allows localities to require assessments of other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry
news_headline: Virginia hits data centers with new energy tax and cracks down on water and noise
news_summary: Virginia has approved new regulations for data centers, including a permit process for high energy use facilities that requires site assessments for noise impacts on homes and schools. Localities can also demand assessments of potential impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
